The CD approval above (2026-10-25) predates these amendments and this ratification and has not been re-run. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
12	> **Re-review (2026-10-27)**: 3 BLOCKING findings and the RECOMMENDED batch applied under the delegated rulings R1 (restore epoch: Save/Load owns the persisted value, the kernel owns the derivation `rng_derive_epoch` and `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE`), R2 (the kernel stamps `seq`; callers attach an echoed `correlation`) and R3 (the completion-sentinel callable contract through `ctx`); no user ruling is reversed. Open Questions 23 (chest-lamp aim latency) and 24 (cross-GDD adjustments) record what this GDD could not decide or edit. The CD approval is still not re-run. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
13	> **Re-review 2 (2026-10-28)**: cross-GDD fixes under G6 and delegated rulings R12–R14 and R21 (user delegated all remaining calls): `restore_epoch` lives in Save/Load's per-slot `slot_epoch.bin`, is made durable in a staging step before `request_restore` and is carried by a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation (CR-8, CR-15, D.10, KRN-EPO-04/05); the kernel rebuilds the binding table's `PlayerId → entities` half inside `LOADING` from registered binding sources (CR-7, KRN-BIND-01..04); a published `block_hash` read and the `canonical_encode` helper (D.12, KRN-HASH-03); the Graph's 0 / 2 / 4 stagger with Suit at (6, 2) (D.2, Section E, KRN-HOOK-01); reference machines RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK named (Open Question 22 closed); Open Question 23 resolved. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
14	
15	## Summary
16	
17	The Command & Simulation Layer is the thin kernel every other system runs inside: a fixed 60 Hz tick, a single door through which every change to the game's state passes as an authority-checked, peer-stamped **command**, a registry of **state blocks** that domain systems own and the kernel never does, and a once-per-tick **change notification** that presentation reads but can never write back through. The player never sees it; what they get from it is a ship that cannot lie — gauges and sprites may be hallucinated, but there is exactly one authoritative truth beneath them, and every command is judged against it. The kernel does not make that truth visible — how, when and at what cost the player learns why a command failed is priced by Interaction, Sanity and the HUD under Pillar 4's verification rule. It exists so that *The World Never Lies* and *Sanity Rewrites Reality* are structural rather than aspirational, and so that co-op can be added later without a rewrite: single-player is simply the host with one local peer.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Foundation` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `None` (upstream); 26 downstream systems named in the Dependencies table (23 hard — 16 with a systems-index edge, 7 presentation consumers whose edges are still to be added — and 3 soft), all MVP/VS systems register with or read it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier "16" counted only the hard rows that already had an index edge)*. **Section letters used throughout** (the template's order): A Overview, B Player Fantasy, C Detailed Design (C.3 = its Interactions table), D Formulas, E Edge Cases, F Dependencies, G Tuning Knobs, H Acceptance Criteria
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	The Command & Simulation Layer is the thin kernel every other system of The Synaptic Sea runs inside. It advances the simulation at a fixed tick, accepts every change to the game's state as a **command** carrying the identity of the peer that issued it, checks that peer's authority, validates the command against current state, applies it or rejects it with a reason, and then tells presentation what changed. It owns no domain state of its own: the Life-Support Graph, the ship layout, suit vitals, Attention, sanity and the rest each register their own **state block** with the kernel's registry and define their own command handlers. The kernel's job is to be the one door through which truth changes.
24	
25	The player never sees this system; they interact with it only through the systems built on it — every weld, every valve turned, every step taken is a command the kernel admitted. It is automatic from the player's point of view and invisible when it works.
26	
27	It exists for two reasons that are both pillars. First, **The World Never Lies** needs one authoritative truth: if any system could mutate state directly, two readers could disagree about whether a pipe is leaking, and the honest-world promise would be unenforceable. Second, **Sanity Rewrites Reality** needs a wall: the Perception Filter and every other presentation script may *read* simulation state and write only what is drawn, never what is true. The kernel is that wall made structural rather than aspirational, and its registry is also the hook the Save/Load contract and the true-value Debug Overlay hang from. The game would lose, without it, the ability to add co-op later without a rewrite (TD-FEASIBILITY: authority discipline from day one — in single-player the local peer simply *is* the host) and the guarantee that a hallucination can never corrupt the ship.
28	
29	**Design-level only.** Whether the kernel is an autoload, how commands are encoded, and how change notification is delivered are implementation choices → **becomes an ADR** (authority model). *(Framing: technical infrastructure, no ADR yet to cite, no direct player fantasy — selected as the recommended options for a `Core`/`Foundation` system under `autonomous` automation.)*
30

90	| `submission_id` | Kernel metadata, never payload-borne: a kernel-unique counter stamped at ISSUED, before admission, so even a rejected submit has one; it is the `result_id` of the command's result (CR-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
91	
92	*Discrete commands vs continuous intents.* If the sim must log, validate, save or replay it, it is a command (examples; each type's owner GDD is authoritative: Controller `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, `toggle_beam`; Interaction `begin_cut` (module salvage, V8), `begin_patch`, `cancel_channel`, `pickup`, `drop`, `set_switch`, `field_check`; Modular Ship Assembly `begin_weld` (declared by Interaction, registered by Assembly), `begin_seam_cut`, `install_module` and the `SYSTEM`-only completions `weld` / `seam_cut` (registry: `assembly_commands`; there is no `remove_module` — it is reserved and unregistered, and V8 salvage is the only removal); Suit `equip_tool` (its only type); Web Map & Transit `pod_hop`, `berth`, `unberth` and the `SYSTEM`-only `pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth_step`, `web_reconcile` (registry: `web_commands`). `interact` is an input action, not a command type, and `use_item` has no owner and is not a command *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, suit-and-equipment, modular-ship-assembly and web-map-and-transit)*). What the stick is doing *right now* is an intent: intents are commands too, but a type may declare `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` — coalescing happens at admission over the unfrozen queue, keyed `(type, actor, issuer_peer)`, the older command becoming `Superseded` — and the input adapter sends one only when the quantised value changes — a few per second, never one per tick. Edge-triggered inputs (press, release, confirm) must declare `coalesce = NONE` or taps are lost. Movement integration runs inside the sim: Body's `body.integrate` hook (divisor 1, P3) reads the current intent and integrates ship-local kinematics (CR-13), so a move intent takes effect one tick after it is submitted, like every command; there is no physics-side integration at MVP, and position ownership is settled (Body owns it; the Controller owns intent and facing) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` every command is round-tripped through serialization before dispatch, even locally; one that cannot survive is a violation (CR-19). **Submit is fire-and-forget and never calls back**: `submit()` returns nothing and invokes no callback, handler or subscriber, so it is safe to call from any handler, hook or result handler; its only outcome is one result record appended to the kernel's result buffer (CR-5), delivered at the next flush and identified by `result_id` — a remote issuer could never get a synchronous answer, so the local one doesn't either *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `submit()` takes the optional `correlation` and returns nothing, not even a receipt: the caller learns the outcome only from the result record, which carries its `correlation` back, so "fire-and-forget" is literally true and `seq` stays the kernel's. The API shape is `submit(type, payload, actor = none, correlation = 0)` on an `INPUT_SURFACE` handle and `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)` for hooks (a hook needs no correlation: it never receives a result) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*.
93	
94	**Payload whitelist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 'Plain' is a recursive `Variant.Type` whitelist checked at admission: `NIL`, `BOOL`, `INT`, `FLOAT` (finite only — `NaN` and `±inf` are `MALFORMED`; the same finite check applies to **each component of a `VECTOR2` and each element of `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array`**, which the walk visits in O(n) bounded by `MAX_PAYLOAD` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `STRING`, `STRING_NAME`, `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, the `Packed{Byte,Int32,Int64,Float32,Float64,String,Vector2}Array` types, and `ARRAY`/`DICTIONARY` of the same, to a depth cap `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` = 8 (which also rejects a self-containing container). Dictionary keys must be `INT`, `STRING` or `STRING_NAME` and **all keys of one dictionary must share one type** (mixed keys have no canonical order, D.12). Anything else — an `Object`, `NodePath`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, a non-whitelisted `Variant.Type`, a non-finite float, a depth-9 nesting, mixed dictionary keys — is `MALFORMED`; the size bound is measured as `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` after the walk passes. Immediate *acknowledgement* (a tool sound, a hand animation, a linear progress bar starting) is presentation's job and happens in the same frame; the sim confirms on the next tick. The latency bounds are stated once, in Game Feel and D.4.
95	
96	**CR-5. Command lifecycle and the exactly-one-result guarantee.** Every command reaches exactly one terminal state and emits exactly one result record (identified by `result_id`; delivered to its issuer unless it is `SYSTEM`-origin, see Result identity and delivery below). Stages: *Issued* → *Admission* (kernel state accepts commands; type registered; **origin allowed for the type — known at admission, so rejected there**; queue not full; `seq` not a duplicate — gaps are accepted and counted, not rejected; issuer rate limit; payload plain) → *Queued* → *Authority check* in P2 (origin re-checked as a defence in depth; if the type declares `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, the binding table says the issuer controls `actor`; age ≤ the type's `max_age_ticks`) → *Validate* (owner's side-effect-free `validate(cmd, views, ctx)`: it reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)` — a domain reason — and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; its return value carries no outcome, CR-19(a)/(b)) → *Apply* (`apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, ending with `return ctx.complete()`; infallible by contract once validate passed, CR-9) → terminal: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)*
97	
98	| Terminal | Meaning |
99	|----------|---------|
100	| `Applied` | Effects are in state as of tick T (a command dispatched earlier in a tick that then faults is still `Applied`, with `detail.uncommitted = 1`) |
101	| `Rejected(reason)` | No effect |
102	| `Dropped(reason)` | Never evaluated: a reload, a shutdown or a fault flushed it — `RELOAD`, `SHUTDOWN`, `FAULTED` (the last added so G5 holds on the defect path). Includes the not-yet-dispatched commands of a faulting tick's batch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
103	| `Faulted(code)` | Evaluated, and its `validate` or `apply` (or a mutator it called) reported a fault through the fault channel (CR-19): effects may be partial and are unreachable to presentation. Exactly one command per fault — the cause. Distinct from `Rejected` (not 'no effect') and `Dropped` (not 'never evaluated') *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
104	| `Superseded` | Coalesced away by a newer command of a coalescing type |
105	
106	Kernel reject reasons are a closed set: `NOT_ACCEPTING`, `PAUSED`, `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, `QUEUE_FULL`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `DUPLICATE_SEQ`, `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `STALE`, `MALFORMED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` — domain codes are namespaced and owned by the registering system (Interaction's set, e.g. `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `PRECONDITION`, `BUSY`, is its GDD's). The result record carries `result_id`, `issuer_peer`, `origin`, `seq`, `correlation`, `ok`, `reason`, `subject` (the target the rejection refers to), an optional `detail` dictionary of numbers, and `tick` — **never display strings** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `result_id` and `origin` added)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2: `correlation` added, echoed unchanged from the submit)*. Presentation maps reasons to sound, shake or tooltip. **Reason codes are computed from true state and the kernel never filters them.** That is the whole of the kernel's claim. Whether, when and how cheaply a reason reaches the player is *not* the kernel's: Interaction, Sanity and the HUD own it and must obey Pillar 4's cost rule (a check costs time, risk or trust) — for example surfacing a `PRECONDITION` only after channel time has been spent, or only through diegetic feedback rather than an instant tooltip. *Design test (CD-GDD-ALIGN):* if a rejection lets the player falsify a hallucination at zero time, risk or trust cost, the presentation of that rejection is wrong — not the kernel. A command *aborted mid-channel* (power drops during a cut) is reported by the channel owner through state change, not through the command result. The kernel never retries.
107	
108	**Result identity and delivery** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A result is identified by `result_id` (the command's `submission_id`). A local issuer correlates by the `correlation` it attached to the submit (echoed unchanged; the caller's own uniqueness, not the kernel's), never by `seq`, which a local caller neither chooses nor learns *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` is unique among results **except** `DUPLICATE_SEQ` rejections, which by definition repeat an earlier command's `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` and are told apart by `result_id` and `reason`; only a test or remote ingress can produce one (see the `seq` row of CR-4). Every terminal result — admission rejections, `Superseded`, P2 results, `Dropped(...)`, `Faulted` — is appended to the kernel's **result buffer** in the order it occurs; `submit()` itself never delivers. The buffer is flushed (a) at P5 of every tick, after the change batch, and (b) by the driver once per rendered frame after that frame's ticks, **in every kernel state** (`BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`, and an idle frame with no tick), so `NOT_ACCEPTING`, `PAUSED`, `Dropped(RELOAD|SHUTDOWN|FAULTED)` and every other result always have a delivery point. A flush swaps the buffer out before delivering: whatever a result handler submits (the STALE resubmit of Section E, for example) is admitted normally, and any result it produces lands in the fresh buffer and is delivered at the next flush, never recursively — a handler that resubmits on every rejection costs one result per flush and cannot loop. Results go to the issuing `INPUT_SURFACE`'s result handler and to the diagnostics log. **`SYSTEM`-origin results are never delivered to a subscriber or to the submitting owner** (owners never subscribe, CR-10); they go to the command log and the diagnostics counters only, and an owner that needs the outcome reads state. **Fault semantics (a designer decision, not an implementer detail)**: when the kernel faults, each command already dispatched in the faulting tick whose `apply` completed receives `Applied` with `detail.uncommitted = 1` (its effects are in the live blocks although P4 never ran); the faulting command receives `Faulted(code)`; every not-yet-dispatched batch command and every pending command receives `Dropped(FAULTED)`; all are buffered at the fault transition and delivered at the next frame flush.
109	
110	**CR-6. Registration at boot, then frozen.** Block, command-type, hook, diagnostics-channel and binding-source registration are legal only in `BOOTING` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from debug-overlay-true-values (E-DO-38))* (a block may declare one optional `binding_source` callable, CR-7; one registered after `BOOTING` is refused like every other registration *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); after `BOOTING → LOADING` the registries are immutable until shutdown. Registration is an explicit declaration by the composition root, not discovery via the scene tree. Duplicate IDs, unknown types, missing owners and hook cycles fail boot loudly in every build. A command type registered without `allowed_origins`, `actor_binding`, `coalesce` or `max_age_ticks` (**no silent defaults**: an omitted `actor_binding` must never mean 'no ownership check'), a block registered without `class`, `gameplay`, `repl_hint` or `persist`, a type whose `writes_blocks` names an unregistered block, and an `allowed_when_paused` type whose `writes_blocks` names any `gameplay = true` block likewise fail boot (`BOOTING → FAULTED`) naming the registration. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A type with `coalesce ≠ NONE` that allows both origins fails boot (`COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN`), because the supersession key carries no origin (D.8); and the joint memory assertion of Section G constraint 8 is checked here *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
111	
112	**CR-7. Authority model (behaviour).** The host is the sole authority: only a `HOST` kernel ticks and applies; a `MIRROR` never applies. Each command type's owner declares `allowed_origins ⊆ {PLAYER, SYSTEM}` and `actor_binding ∈ {NONE, OWNED_BY_ISSUER}` — both mandatory (CR-6) — and `allowed_origins` is checked at admission, with a P2 re-check as defence in depth. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `SYSTEM` commands never arrive from a network; remote ingress always stamps `PLAYER`. The kernel holds a **binding table** — `peer_id → PlayerId` and `PlayerId → {controlled entity IDs}` — as identity data, not domain state; the table has two halves with different lifetimes *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6 (user delegated all remaining calls): the kernel owns the rebuild; closes Body Open Question 30)*. **(a) `peer_id → PlayerId`** is session state: it is mutated only through a host-only API called by the session owner (a boot step in MVP: `HOST_PEER_ID` 1 → PlayerId 1; Co-op Session in VS-B), and a restore, a death restart or a new game never touches it and never resets any issuer's `seq` or `last_seq`. **(b) `PlayerId → {controlled entity IDs}`** is derived from saved state and is never saved: **the kernel rebuilds it itself as the last step of every pass through `LOADING`** (`request_restore` and `request_new_game` alike), after the last `post_restore()` and the K-4 hash check and before the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition. The rebuild clears half (b) entirely, then calls each registered **binding source** (CR-6, CR-8) in ascending `block_id` order — with `ctx`, as a pure read of its owner's block, under no `WriteScope`, ending `return ctx.complete()` — which delivers `[(player_id, entity_id)]` in ascending order through `ctx.put`, and binds every pair. The kernel checks *who*; owners validate *whether the world allows it*; the kernel encodes no game rules. For friendly harm the kernel checks only issuer→actor ownership; the "attacker below the sanity threshold" gate is Interaction's `validate` calling Sanity's query on the actor's authoritative sanity level (a `SIM` block), never on anyone's perception.
113	
114	**CR-8. `scope` ∈ {`SHARED`, `PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId}; `gameplay` (bool, mandatory: true when a gameplay verb can change the block; false only for settings, menu and save-request state — the CR-16 paused-write test) and `interpolated` (bool, default false: when true the kernel calls the owner's `commit_baseline()` at P4 so the previous/current pair rolls exactly once per tick, and after a restore or an owner-declared teleport/reset the owner calls `snap_baseline(key)` so presentation never interpolates across a discontinuity) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `repl_hint` ∈ {`HOST_ONLY`, `SHARED_SUMMARY`, `OWNER_PRIVATE`} — mandatory now though unused until VS-B, so no block ever ships without the decision; `snapshot(ctx)` (delivers its plain data through `ctx.put(payload)` and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; canonical state only, deterministic ordering, entity references by stable ID, no derived caches; **the payload is a deep copy** — `duplicate_deep()` for Dictionary/Array, `duplicate()` for Packed arrays, which GDScript passes by reference — never a reference into live state); `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` (whole-block replace; **copies in** and never retains a reference to `data`, so two restores from one payload cannot alias; the owner migrates from `stored_version`; The kernel receives it as an argument of `request_restore` and `request_new_game` (CR-15, CR-18), holds it read-only for the session and exposes it in the `kernel.clock` **read view** as the triple `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`, so a hook reads it purely, as a read of kernel state (H9). # Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at

> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`

672	- **If a command's `actor` was destroyed earlier in the same tick (by an earlier command or, for a hook-submitted command, by last tick's P3)**: the kernel's authority check consults only the binding table, which is identity data and is not touched by domain destruction, so authority *passes* if the issuer is still bound to that entity ID; the owner's `validate` then fails on a missing entity and the result is `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` (Interaction's `INVALID_TARGET` or equivalent). content.thinking: All residual counts check out clean, with just the one intended new wording for KRN-BIND-04 remaining as expected. I'm ready to return the registry request for kernel_binding_table.

applied: (1) CR-7 (L112): half (b) renamed to `PlayerId → {(source block_id, entity_id)}` in both places (the two-half dash and the bold (b) heading). Added the rule that each pair is stored under the source's own block_id, with the block-local-ID rationale. Replaced the conflict sentence with the keyed wording: two PlayerIds for one key, or a duplicate triple, is BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT, and checks run only within one source. Added the `actor_source` authority rule after the allowed_origins/actor_binding sentence, with `body.state` for avatar-acting types and `emitter.state` for toggle_beam. I grepped the Body and Emitter GDDs read-only: both block_ids are real. Single-player now reads {(`body.state`, avatar actor_id), (`emitter.state`, beam_id)}, with a 'both may be 1' note and the 'Resolved 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix (G6)' record. Added an inline registry-request marker. Each edit is marked *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
(2) CR-4 `actor` row (L85) rewritten as requested: the actor ID lives in the ID space of the type's actor_source block.

(3) CR-6 (L110): the mandatory list now includes three cases that fail boot with ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID: an OWNED_BY_ISSUER type with no actor_source, an actor_source that names a block with no binding_source, and a NONE type that declares an actor_source.
(4) CR-8 (L114): after 'the kernel allocates none.' added that IDs are unique only within their block and that the kernel keys cross-block references by (block_id, entity_id).
(5) Section E: L672 now reads 'still bound to the key `(actor_source, actor)`'. Added the bullet on two sources delivering the same entity number (Body (1,1) and Emitter (1,1)) after the L734 bullet.
(6) AC L930: the GIVEN now has `actor_source = A` and peer 1 bound to `(A, 7)` only.
(7) AC L965: added the actor_source boot failures (ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID). The tag already read [CR-6, CR-7, CR-8], which covers the requested [CR-6, CR-7], so I kept it.
(8) KRN-BIND-01: the fixture type declares `actor_source = A`, and the expected half is now {1: {(A, 5)}, 2: {(A, 9)}}.
(9) KRN-BIND-03: now reads 'key (A, 5) bound to PlayerId 1' and '(A, 5) is absent'.
(10) KRN-BIND-04: now covers one binding source yielding [(1, 5), (2, 5)], or the same pair twice [(1, 5), (1, 5)].
(11) New KRN-BIND-05 inserted after KRN-BIND-04, verbatim as requested.
(12) L13 Re-review 2 summary: KRN-BIND-01..05, plus 'keyed `(source block_id, entity_id)`, with each `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` type declaring `actor_source`'. L1104 closing stories: KRN-BIND-01..05.
(13) The GDD has no registry-request list section, so I did not invent one. The registry request is returned in registry_requests below, and CR-7 carries an inline marker naming it.

Consistency follow-ups under rule C/G3, all marked amended: KRN-BIND-02 '{1: {5}}' is now '{1: {(A, 5)}}' (fixture block A named). The old 'PlayerId → entities' shorthand at L13, L149 (States), L667 (Section E seq rule), L734 and KRN-BIND-01 now reads `PlayerId → {(block_id, entity_id)}`. The CR-5 authority-check stage now reads 'controls the key `(actor_source, actor)`'.

Open Question 24 (cross-GDD adjustments): added one line saying every GDD that registers an OWNED_BY_ISSUER type must declare actor_source or fail boot with ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID. Those GDDs are Player Controller, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Modular Ship Assembly and Emitter State; I confirmed this by grepping OWNED_BY_ISSUER across design/gdd. The line is needed because those GDDs own the type registrations, and without it each of those types fails boot.
Header 'Last Updated' line: added one short note for this pass.

registry_requests.reason: CR-7/CR-8 cross-GDD fix (G6). Entity IDs are block-local, and Body next_actor_id and Emitter next_emitter_id both start at 1. Bare keys raised a false BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT on every single-player boot.

registry_requests.reason: Conflict detection is now per source key (CR-7, KRN-BIND-04/05).

registry_requests.name: kernel_binding_table
registry_requests.change: add attribute actor_source: "mandatory iff actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER; names a block with a registered binding_source (body.state for avatar-acting types, emitter.state for toggle_beam); P2 authority passes iff (actor_source(type), actor) in half_b[PlayerId(issuer_peer)]; a missing actor_source, one naming a block without a binding_source, or one declared on a NONE type fails boot with ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID"
registry_requests.reason: This is new kernel registration surface (CR-6, CR-7, AC L965, KRN-BIND-05). It lets OWNED_BY_ISSUER tell an avatar actor from a beam with the same number.
